references.text: Moses describes clean and unclean animals in the law, which Jesus addresses in Mark 7:19 by declaring all foods clean.
David speaks about purity of heart, echoing Jesus' point that what enters a person does not make them unclean, but what comes out of the heart.
Isaiah criticizes the people's false piety, reflecting Jesus' critique of the Pharisees' attitudes in Mark 7.
Jesus teaches that it is not what goes into the mouth that makes a person unclean, but what comes out of the heart, paralleling Mark 7:19.
Peter's vision of clean and unclean animals and the message that God has declared all foods clean underscores Jesus' teaching in Mark 7:19.
God's command to Peter not to call anything unclean that God has cleansed echoes Jesus' words in Mark 7:19 that all foods are clean.
